new.title: Photograph the Plönlein fork in Rothenburg
new.desc: The Plönlein is a small triangular square where the Kobolzeller Steige and Spitalgasse split, framed by a half-timbered house and the Siebersturm. It is Rothenburg's best-known photo spot.
new.tip: Come early morning or after 18:00 to avoid tour-group crowds.

new.title: Climb the Rathaus tower above Marktplatz
new.desc: The town hall tower in Rothenburg is about 61 m tall, and the top room gives a view over most of the old town and the Tauber valley.
new.tip: Entry costs a couple of euros; the climb is steep and narrow.
new.q: Rathaus, Marktplatz 1, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: See the Holy Blood altar in St. James' Church
new.desc: St. Jakob holds the Holy Blood reredos carved by Tilman Riemenschneider between 1500 and 1505. The Gothic church is Rothenburg's main parish church.
new.tip: Entry is ticketed; the altar is in the west gallery.
new.q: St.-Jakobs-Kirche, Klingengasse 1, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Visit the Medieval Crime Museum
new.desc: The museum shows about 1,000 years of legal history, with instruments of punishment, torture devices and scold's bridles. It occupies the former Johanniter commandery at Burggasse 3-5.
new.tip: Allow an hour; the last entry is 45 minutes before closing, and times vary seasonally.
new.q: Mittelalterliches Kriminalmuseum, Burggasse 3, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Browse the Käthe Wohlfahrt Christmas Museum
new.desc: Rothenburg's Weihnachtsmuseum shows the history of Christmas decorations and customs, next to the year-round Christmas shop of Käthe Wohlfahrt.
new.tip: Open all year, so it works as a rainy-day stop in summer too.
new.q: Deutsches Weihnachtsmuseum, Herrngasse 1, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Walk the Burggarten above the Tauber valley
new.desc: The Burggarten lies on the site of the former imperial castle at the western edge of the old town. It has views down to the Tauber valley.
new.tip: Free to enter; go at sunset for the valley light.
new.q: Burggarten, Burggasse, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Walk Rothenburg's medieval town wall
new.desc: The old town is ringed by a wall with covered walkways and towers such as the Klingentor; the eastern stretches were rebuilt after bomb damage in 1945. Large parts of it can be walked.
new.tip: Free to walk; start at the Rödertor and follow the loop in about an hour.

new.title: Follow the Night Watchman tour through Rothenburg
new.desc: The night watchman leads a roughly one-hour tour of lanes and legends, starting at the Marktplatz. Tours run in German and English, and the English tour has been offered at 20:00.
new.tip: Adults paid about 8 euro in 2024 and children under 12 were free; confirm the time with Rothenburg Tourismus.

new.title: Shop the Reiterlesmarkt Christmas market
new.desc: Rothenburg's Christmas market, the Reiterlesmarkt, fills the Marktplatz and nearby lanes in the weeks before Christmas, in front of the half-timbered old town.
new.tip: Go on a weekday afternoon; weekends are crowded.

new.title: Eat Franconian dishes at Zur Höll
new.desc: Zur Höll is a restaurant in a building said to date from around AD 900, claimed as the oldest in Rothenburg. Fodor's lists it among the town's restaurants.
new.tip: Try the regional Schäufele or a Franconian plate; book ahead in summer.
new.q: Restaurant Zur Höll, Burggasse 8, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Try a Schneeball at Bäckerei Friedel
new.desc: The Schneeball is Rothenburg's deep-fried dough pastry coated in sugar or chocolate. Bäckerei-Konditorei-Café Friedel on the Markt is listed as a bakery known for them.
new.tip: Buy a plain one first, then try chocolate or nougat.
new.q: Bäckerei Friedel, Markt 8, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Eat potato dishes at the Gasthof Rödertor Kartoffelstube
new.desc: The Kartoffelstube at Gasthof Rödertor builds its menu around potatoes, from dumplings to potato-base pizza, plus meat dishes such as Schäufele.
new.tip: Ask for the Schäufele; reviews call it tender.
new.q: Gasthof Rödertor, Rödergasse, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Order roast goose leg at Gasthof Goldener Greifen
new.desc: This Gasthof in the old town serves Franconian cooking such as roast goose leg with red cabbage and potato dumplings, according to Frommer's.
new.tip: Goose is a cool-season dish here; ask about the day's specials.
new.q: Gasthof Goldener Greifen, Obere Schmiedgasse 5, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

new.title: Stroll Dinkelsbühl's old town to St. George's Minster
new.desc: Dinkelsbühl is a walled free imperial city with an almost complete medieval ring of towers and gates, including the Wörnitztor. The late Gothic hall church of St. Georg stands at its centre.
new.tip: Walk the town wall at dusk, then pause at the Weinmarkt.

new.title: Tour the Residenz Ansbach state rooms
new.desc: The Residenz was the seat of the Margraves of Brandenburg-Ansbach. Its Prunkräume can only be seen on a guided tour of about 50 minutes, run by the Bavarian Palace Administration.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; tour times change seasonally, see schloesser.bayern.de. The Hofgarten and Orangerie café are open to all.

new.title: Walk the boardwalks above the Roman baths in Weißenburg
new.desc: The Roman Thermae of Weißenburg are among the best-preserved bath complexes in southern Germany, now under a tent roof with walkways.
new.tip: Combine with the RömerMuseum on a combined ticket.
new.q: Römische Thermen, Am Römerbad 17a, Weißenburg in Bayern

new.title: Explore the Wülzburg Renaissance fortress
new.desc: The Wülzburg is a Renaissance fortress on a hill east of Weißenburg; it has a 143 m deep well hewn into the rock, and Charles de Gaulle was held here in the First World War.
new.tip: Guided tours run through Museen Weißenburg.

new.title: Meet Juravenator at the Jura-Museum in Eichstätt
new.desc: The Jura-Museum inside the Willibaldsburg shows Jurassic fossils from the Solnhofen quarries, including marine reptiles, pterosaurs and the small dinosaur Juravenator starki.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; open 9-18 in summer, 10-16 in winter.

new.title: Visit Eichstätt Cathedral
new.desc: The cathedral combines Romanesque origins with later Gothic, Baroque and Rococo elements, and anchors Eichstätt's prince-bishop townscape.
new.tip: Free to enter; wander the Baroque streets around the Residenzplatz afterwards.

new.title: Try on Roman gear at the Römer und Bajuwaren Museum
new.desc: The museum in the outer ward of Burg Kipfenberg covers the Limes, Roman rule and the arrival of the Baiuvarii in the Altmühl valley. It is also a Limes info point.
new.tip: Visitors can try on Roman equipment; open daily 10-16 per museum listings.
new.q: Römer und Bajuwaren Museum, Burg 1, Kipfenberg

new.title: Climb to the ruins of Burg Pappenheim
new.desc: The castle is a high medieval spur castle from the 11th century above Pappenheim. The keep gives a view over the town and the Altmühl valley.
new.tip: Open April to October; entry was about 4 euro at last listing.

new.title: See folk art at the Fränkisches Museum Feuchtwangen
new.desc: The museum is described by the town as one of the finest folk-art museums in southern Germany. ADAC highlights a 1484 altarpiece from the workshop of Michael Wolgemut, Dürer's teacher.
new.tip: Combine with the late Romanesque cloister next door.

new.title: Photograph the Stadtbrille in Amberg
new.desc: The Stadtbrille is a double-arched water gate across the Vils, dated 1454 or 1464 depending on the source. Its reflection makes it look like a pair of glasses, hence the name.
new.tip: Best from the riverbank in the evening.

new.title: Admire St. Martin's Basilica on Amberg's Marktplatz
new.desc: St. Martin is a late Gothic hall church whose 92 m tower has a green cupola; it is the main church of Amberg's old town.
new.tip: Free to enter. The old town survived the Second World War largely intact.

new.title: See fossils at the Bürgermeister-Müller-Museum
new.desc: The museum in Solnhofen shows fossils from the Solnhofen limestone, and offers a children's programme with a treasure hunt in the quarry.
new.tip: Open seven days in summer; the museum also sells tickets for the hobby quarry.

new.title: Visit the former synagogue of Sulzbach
new.desc: The synagogue was rebuilt after the 1822 town fire and consecrated in 1827; since 2013 it is a memorial and documentation centre on Jewish life in the Upper Palatinate.
new.tip: Open by appointment; arrange through the city tourism office.

new.title: Drink house beer and Weib's Töpfle at Weib's Brauhaus
new.desc: Weib's Brauhaus is a half-timbered brewpub in Dinkelsbühl run by a female brewmaster; Lonely Planet names the Weib's Töpfle, pork in beer sauce with croquettes.
new.tip: Open late; closed Tuesdays per one listing.

new.title: Dine in the 1440 Hotel Deutsches Haus in Dinkelsbühl
new.desc: The Hotel Deutsches Haus on the Weinmarkt is a half-timbered hotel in a building dating to 1440, with an Altdeutsches Restaurant serving regional cuisine.
new.tip: Reserve in the evening, especially during the Kinderzeche in July.

new.title: Eat in the beer garden of Braugasthof Trompete in Eichstätt
new.desc: The Braugasthof Trompete has a beer garden for 60 guests, a weekly changing menu of Bavarian specialities and Gutmann beers from Titting.
new.tip: Check the weekly specials board.

new.title: Taste Eichstätt's own beer from Privatbrauerei Hofmühl
new.desc: Privatbrauerei Hofmühl is the only brewery located in Eichstätt itself.
new.tip: Look for Hofmühl on tap in local Gasthäuser.

new.title: Sit in the Bruckmüller courtyard in Amberg
new.desc: Brauerei Bruckmüller is a brewery and Bavarian restaurant with a courtyard beer garden, one of the breweries in the Amberger Bierfest.
new.tip: Open from 11:30; try a house lager with regional dishes.

new.title: Order Schweinebraten at Schloderer Bräu in Amberg
new.desc: Schloderer Bräu is an old-town brewhouse restaurant with three draught beers; a reviewer highlights its roast pork in dark beer sauce.
new.tip: Pair the Schweinebraten with the house dark beer.

new.title: Eat at Haus am See on the Altmühlsee
new.desc: Restaurant Haus am See stands at the Wald-Seezentrum on the Altmühlsee near Gunzenhausen, with lake views and a choice of beers.
new.tip: Check the menu for seasonal carp.

new.title: Look for Altmühltal lamb at Zum Goldenen Lamm in Treuchtlingen
new.desc: Gasthof Zum Goldenen Lamm at Marktstraße 16 is a riverside inn with a restaurant. The Altmühltaler Lamm is a regional quality label.
new.tip: Ask whether lamb is on the menu; confirm by phone.
new.q: Gasthof Zum Goldenen Lamm, Marktstraße 16, Treuchtlingen

new.title: Try Altmühltaler Weiderind at Hotel-Gasthof Sonne in Pappenheim
new.desc: The Sonne is listed among Pappenheim places serving Altmühltaler Weiderind, regional pasture-raised beef.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to Burg Pappenheim.

new.title: Join the Kinderzeche festival in Dinkelsbühl
new.desc: The Kinderzeche is a historical children's and heritage festival with a play in the Schranne, a parade on Sunday and a funfair on the Schießwasen; it is UNESCO intangible heritage. The 2026 edition ran 17 to 26 July.
new.tip: Tickets via kinderzeche.de; book early.

new.title: See open-air theatre at the Kreuzgangspiele Feuchtwangen
new.desc: The Feuchtwangen Kreuzgangspiele have been staged in the late Romanesque cloister each year since 1949.
new.tip: Box office at Marktplatz 2; check the programme.

new.title: Cruise Brombachsee on the MS Brombachsee trimaran
new.desc: The MS Brombachsee is billed as Europe's first and largest passenger trimaran on an inland lake, with five piers: Ramsberg, Absberg, Enderndorf, Allmannsdorf and Pleinfeld/Wald. A cruise lasts about 1.5 hours.
new.tip: Operator phone 09144 92 70 50; check season dates.

new.title: Swim at the Strandbad on Großer Brombachsee
new.desc: The Großer Brombachsee has a Strandbad and a sailing school, and Ramsberg has a large inland sailing harbour.
new.tip: Season is summer; bring a sunhat.

new.title: Paddle the Altmühl from Treuchtlingen to Pappenheim
new.desc: The Altmühl is one of Bavaria's calmest paddling rivers; Kanuuh in Treuchtlingen rents canoes, with a 15 km stretch to Pappenheim and weirs to portage.
new.tip: Best April to October; take the train back.

new.title: Hire a boat from Bootsverleih Altmühl in Pappenheim
new.desc: Bootsverleih Altmühl at Beckstraße 34 in Pappenheim is one of the Altmühl canoe outfitters between Treuchtlingen and Dollnstein.
new.tip: Phone ahead; return transport can be arranged.

new.title: Split slate for fossils at the Besuchersteinbruch Mühlheim
new.desc: The visitor quarry at Mühlheim near Mörnsheim offers 60-minute guided tours with tools included, then lets you hunt fossils yourself (2019 information).
new.tip: Group tours need at least five people; confirm.

new.title: Dig for fossils in the Solnhofen hobby quarry
new.desc: The Hobbysteinbruch near Solnhofen lets visitors search the Mörnsheim beds for fossils; the museum rents tools and sells tickets.
new.tip: Open about April to October, 9-17.

new.title: Walk the Altmühlsee shore to the Vogelinsel
new.desc: The Altmühlsee has a 12 km shore path, and its Vogelinsel is a significant protected area for migratory birds, explored from Muhr am See.
new.tip: Bring binoculars in spring and autumn.

new.title: Visit the Luftmuseum in Amberg
new.desc: The Luftmuseum is in the Klösterl, called Engelsburg, from the early 14th century. Artist Wilhelm Koch founded it in 2006 with the Luftmuseum e.V. to show art about air.
new.tip: Amberg has called itself Luftkunstort since 2009.
